task_title: Enemy projectile telegraph (aim-lock + visual cue + AI dodge)

plan_review.notes: Adversarial review across 4 rounds. Round 1: 8 concerns (5 blocking) - sentinel/recycle collision, cadence change, cancellation coverage, virtual-projectile dodge fidelity, perception gating, debug-radius plumbing, weak determinism coverage, accuracy-roll timing. Rounds 2-4 resolved all + surfaced 2 more: (1) sentinel uses -1 (not 0) written explicitly in spawnBehaviorEnemy set(EnemyBehavior,{telegraphMs: options?.telegraphMs ?? -1}) at every spawn, since clearEntityStores zeroes typed-array slots on every createEntity call not just recycled EIDs; (2) cadence change (cooldown+telegraphMs) accepted as intentional additive consequence documented in ADR, not compensated; (3) 5 cancellation call sites identified in enemyAISystem per-enemy loop; (4) virtual-projectile dodge reads explicit locked telegraphOriginX/Y + telegraphDirX/Y stored once at telegraph start, used identically by render cue, AI dodge math, and actual fire-time spawn (lockedOrigin + lockedDir * MUZZLE_OFFSET) - correctness independent of live-position drift from separation/knockback/unstuck; (5) perception gating via canPerceiveWorldPosition on new telegraph-dodge loop; (6) debug plumbing scoped to bt-ai-provider.ts only, travel-steering.ts confirmed out of scope; (7) determinism tests added; (8) accuracy roll stays at fire-time (accepted trade-off); (9) stuckFrames forced to 0 every frame while telegraphActive===1, tryUnstuckVelocity gated off for whole window; (10) applySeparation skips writing velocity onto a telegraphing eid. Final verdict: approved.

rounds.notes: Single-model pass against the full branch diff. Explicitly verified all 9 contract-correctness points from the review brief (delay resolution, 0ms parity, cancellation coverage, actual-attack-range danger radius, virtual-projectile-vs-real-fire consistency, EID-recycling sentinel, CLI wiring, test genuineness, createTestWorld() 0ms masking risk). No concerns raised. The 2 real bugs below were caught only by the independent multi-model fan-out (see multi_model_review), which is why both stages are required at this apple tier.

Post-open shepherding: GitHub's automated PR-review pass re-ran on each push while driving PR #1196 to merge and surfaced 10 further genuine issues beyond the pre-merge stages above: telegraph movement-freeze timing, an FOV-gate bypass in the AI dodge path, dead-shooter dodge still firing, stale CLI help text, a PhaserBridge dead-shooter render-cue gap, stale doc test counts, an unbounded-range dodge case, a recycled-EID cleanup bug, an FOV-vs-live-position mismatch, and missing coordinate-pinned test coverage. Each was root-caused, fixed with a regression test, verified (typecheck/lint/verify:fast), committed, and the corresponding review thread replied-to + resolved before the next push.

Further post-open pass (after an update-branch merge with main): (1) bt-ai-provider.ts range-gate hard-rejected candidates the real fire pipeline actually lets land on the step it first exceeds maxRange — fixed by clamping to maxReachableFrames instead of rejecting, with 2 new regression tests; (2) the 250ms default telegraph delay required a broad (>10-run) GitHub-Actions win-rate sweep per AGENTS.md rule 15/rule 12 before it could be treated as balance-validated — dispatched weapon-sweep.yml on main (95.6% win rate) vs. this branch (92.2%), both comfortably above the 90% Floor-1 gate, documented in the handoff's new Balance validation section; (3)+(4) two stale ADR passages (visibility-gate description, 0ms-legacy-parity consequences); (5) stale PR-description test counts. All fixed, verified, committed, and threads replied-to + resolved.

Further post-open pass after the round-3 push: (1) a round-1-era test comment and the handoff's retrospective wrongly cited the raw (unused) src/shared/data/weapons.json fireball projectileSpeed of 4.0 as the runtime value, when both the fire path and the AI dodge math actually call getWeaponDef('fireball') (src/shared/weaponDefs.ts), which hardcodes 0.5 — corrected the test-comment drift math (3 frames / 92.8 total, not 0.375/90.175) and rewrote the handoff's Mistakes Made / Opportunities sections to cite the true runtime source; (2) a PhaserBridge.ts comment claiming only the render cue is FOV-gated was stale since round 2 already gated the AI dodge path identically — corrected; (3) a real bug: the telegraph cue's urgency-pulse sine phase used the absolute renderElapsedMs while its frequency also depends on progress, causing a phase-discontinuity flicker in long-running sessions — fixed by phasing on the telegraph's own relative elapsedMs instead, with a new regression test (tests/unit/phaser-bridge.test.ts) asserting identical pulse alpha for two telegraphs at the same relative-elapsed-since-start but very different absolute render-clock values; (4) this ledger itself was flagged as stale (marking 'clean' after a single recorded round despite the PR/handoff documenting several further rounds of real bug-finding) — addressed by adding rounds 2-4 above so the ledger's account matches the actual multi-round review history. All fixed, verified (tsc/eslint/verify:fast/full affected-suite reruns), committed, and threads replied-to + resolved.

4-way fan-out (3 code-review models + 1 security-review model, gpt-5.4) against the full branch diff. sonnet: no concerns. security (gpt-5.4): no concerns. codex: 2 concerns — (A) enemyAISystem.ts's playerEid===undefined early-return never called cancelEnemyProjectileTelegraph, unlike every other early-exit branch, risking a stale telegraph; (B) bt-ai-provider.ts's telegraphed-virtual-projectile dodge math used the raw locked telegraphOriginX/Y instead of the muzzle-offset-adjusted spawn point that fireEnemyProjectileFrom() actually fires from, a systematic ~0.375-frame drift. gemini independently found the same finding B, corroborating it. Adjudicator (gpt-5.4, xhigh) re-verified both against source, confirmed BOTH VALID with concrete remedies, and confirmed the render cue (PhaserBridge.ts) should stay as-is (intentionally shows locked body position, not the muzzle point). Both fixes applied: (A) added cancelEnemyProjectileTelegraph() call inside the no-player-branch loop; (B) spawnX/Y now computed with ENEMY_PROJECTILE.MUZZLE_OFFSET applied before relativeX/Y. Two new regression tests added (tests/game/enemy-projectile-telegraph.test.ts and tests/game/behavior-tree-ai.test.ts) that fail if either fix is reverted. Full affected-suite re-run + typecheck/lint/verify:fast all green after the fixes.
